pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ai' in rain — 'ay' is usually used at the end of a word, like day and play.
mnemonic: When the /ai/ sound comes at the end of a word, it packs its bags and wears its 'y' boots instead of its 'i' coat. Sunbeam Day always waves goodbye with a big 'ay!' as the sun goes down.

character.name: Sunbeam Day
character.blurb: Sunbeam Day is the last warm ray of sunshine at the end of a bright day, and she only ever appears at the end of a word, just like 'ay'.

formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'y', close together — two letters, one sound.

pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ow' in cow — 'ou' usually appears in the middle of a word.

pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'igh' in night — 'ie' often appears at the end of a word.

pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ee' in tree — 'ea' is very common in the middle of words.

pronunciation_note: Another way to write the /ch/ sound children already know from 'chip' — the t is silent. 'tch' comes straight after a short vowel at the end of a word: catch, fetch, kitchen. (Common exceptions: rich, which, much, such.)

pronunciation_note: The /v/ sound children already know from 'van'. English words hardly ever end in the letter v, so when a word ends with a /v/ sound, an e is added after the v and makes no sound: give, live, have, sleeve.
